text: Most of the day, this screen is off. Turn it on, and it sells you something.

Today turns the Fire TV into something else. A window that follows the light and the weather — it's raining in Brooklyn, so the tiger has its umbrella. One step that's hers. The whole family, at a glance.
She talks to her phone, however it comes out.
It opens already knowing what she's been letting slide.
She never touches the television. A few seconds later, it catches up on its own.
Something she keeps putting off. It asks one question. One — because two is a form.
When she answers, whatever is missing becomes step one.
Underneath, it's broken down, each step with the moment it fits into. But she only ever gets one a day.
Ask it something it doesn't know, and it looks it up, then reads what it found against this family.
Somewhere warm for an eight-month-old. It skips the place that's closed on Saturdays, and hands the choice back.
Press right on the remote, and the same thing opens on the big screen. When, what it costs, whether it suits a baby.
It follows the day, morning to night. At night, it rests too.
No shopping. No feed. No keeping score.
Today. A small tiger who keeps today for you.
